result.title: Evidence-Based Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Language Models
result.summary: Reinforcement learning from terminal answer rewards enables search-augmented language models to interleave reasoning and retrieval without step-level annotations, yet outcome supervision assigns identical credit to every search in a trajectory regardless of whether it retrieved useful information. This limitation is especially severe when all sampled rollouts for a question fail, collapsing group-centered outcome advantages to zero even when trajectories gather markedly different evidence. We present Evidence-based Credit Assignment (ECA), which augments terminal outcome rewards with a training-only auxiliary signal measuring how retrieved documents improve the likelihood of a reference answer. Rather than scoring the full dialogue prefix, ECA queries a frozen snapshot of the current policy under an evidence-only prompt containing solely the question and the deduplicated documents observed so far, isolating the utility of retrieved passages from surface variations in generated thoughts or search queries. Within this framework, we compare two return formulations, ECA-Step (which accumulates step-clipped potential increments) and ECA-Horizon (which preserves the telescoping horizon gain in potential), paired with cross-fold group normalization, novelty gating, and search-local token assignment. Across seven Search QA benchmarks, ECA-Horizon improves strict macro exact match over an outcome-only GRPO baseline by 1.03 and 4.80 percentage points on Qwen2.5-3B- and 7B-Instruct, respectively, outperforming both RLOO and GiGPO. Zero-shot evaluation on MultiHop-RAG further demonstrates strong transfer to multi-hop inference queries.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ECA：用仅含问题与去重后已检索文档的 evidence-only 提示查询冻结策略快照，以文档提升参考答案似然的程度作为训练辅助信号，与终端结果奖励结合，并比较 ECA-Step 与 ECA-Horizon 两种回报形式。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「隔离检索证据效用、区分轨迹中各步贡献」的思路，与 LVR 关注的答案是否真正使用证据、轨迹级贡献分配与监督高度对应；这种剥离生成思维与查询表层差异的探测方式可供核查是否迁移到视觉证据筛选与 latent 轨迹信用分配。
